problem: Existing VLN methods centralize all house environments and user instructions on a server for both seen-environment training and unseen-environment pre-exploration, which ignores user data privacy. Centralized pre-exploration also hinders adaptation to a specific environment, while environment-based pre-exploration suffers from data scarcity and bias.
motivation: Embodied agents observe sensitive information such as house layouts, user speech and activities, so privacy-preserving training is needed for trustworthy deployment. The authors observe that speaker-generated pseudo-instructions are much simpler and differ statistically from human instructions, so a language encoder trained on one environment's pseudo data generalizes poorly. Yet the visual and decision modules benefit from local adaptation.
key_idea: Treat each house as a federated client: train the VLN agent and speaker with federated averaging, and during pre-exploration aggregate only the language encoder across seen and unseen clients while keeping the trajectory encoder and decision module local.
insight: Sharing only the language encoder (24.6% of parameters) retains general language understanding while letting the vision and decision modules adapt locally. This gives +4.2% SR over full-model sharing (Fed-Full) and roughly matches environment-based pre-exploration. Adding seen environments to the federated round brings human-labeled language into the encoder and gives a further ~0.8% SR gain. Centralized pre-exploration is worse than environment-based (3.1% SR gap), which shows adaptation matters more than pooling data.
method: Decentralized federated training: each seen environment is a client that trains locally for τ epochs (3 for Envdrop, 5 for CLIP-ViL) with 20% participation per round; the server aggregates deltas by FedAvg-style sample-weighted averaging with server learning rate η.

Federated speaker: each client trains a local speaker on its own route-instruction pairs; the global speaker with the best BLEU is sent back and generates pseudo-instructions locally for augmented federated agent training.

Federated pre-exploration: unseen-environment clients train on sampled routes plus speaker pseudo-instructions, with 1 local epoch and 50-70% participation. Only language encoder updates are uploaded and aggregated, while the trajectory encoder and decision module stay local.

Fed-Lan+seen: a fraction (0.18) of seen environments also join each pre-exploration round to improve encoder generalization with human-labeled instructions; evaluation uses the local models after local training.

Analysis of the instruction distribution gap: speaker instructions are shorter (length 21.89 vs 29.58 words) with lower variance and simpler verbs than human ones, motivating the shared language encoder.
Privacy levels: a qualitative scale from 0 (centralized data sharing) to 3 (env-based, no sharing), with Fed-Full at 1 and language-encoder sharing at 2 (24.6% of parameters shared).

setting.backbone: Envdrop (Bi-LSTM language encoder + attentive LSTM decoder, trained from scratch) and CLIP-ViL (CLIP visual encoder based agent), both trained with federated learning

setting.observation: panoramic RGB views in the Matterport3D simulator (navigation-graph viewpoints)

results: Federated training matches centralized training on unseen environments (e.g., FedCLIP-ViL SR 53.4 vs CLIP-ViL 53.6 on R2R; FedEnvdrop 47.5 vs Envdrop 44.5), while trailing on seen environments by ~2.8% SR. Federated pre-exploration Fed-Lan+seen reaches 69.5 SR (CLIP-ViT) and 68.3 SR (Envdrop) on R2R val-unseen, beating centralized (65.3/64.8) and environment-based (68.9/67.4) pre-exploration.
limitations: Does not consider adversarial privacy attacks (e.g., model inversion) that could recover data from shared updates, and privacy is only ordinal and qualitative.
Only evaluated on two non-pretrained baselines (Envdrop, CLIP-ViL) and simulated federation; VLN pre-training privacy is not addressed.
Federated training needs more steps and communication rounds than centralized training (8.25×10^4 vs 3.56×10^4), and the gains over environment-based pre-exploration are small (~0.8-1% SR).
